summary: This specification updates OLSRv2 with an optimization that improves how routing multipoint relays are selected. The optimization retains full interoperability between implementations with and without it.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC adds an optional way for OLSRv2 routers to remove some unnecessary routing relays. Routers using the optimization still interoperate with routers that do not.

questions: what is the olsrv2 mpr optimization
does olsrv2 mpr optimization break interoperability
when can an olsrv2 router remove an mpr
subtitle: An optional optimization that can remove unnecessary routing multipoint relays.

tldr.problem: OLSRv2's routing multipoint relay selection can retain relays that are unnecessary when link metrics are considered.
tldr.mechanism: A router MAY remove certain selected relays when the metric distance through an existing relay is shorter than the direct distance.
tldr.outcome: The optimization may reduce message size and quantity while retaining interoperability; it updates RFC 7181.

today: RFC 7187 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 7181. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 7187.

sections.title: The Optimization and Its Scope
sections.content:
OLSRv2 is a proactive link-state routing protocol designed for mobile ad hoc networks. It uses link metrics, and earlier rationale described removing some routing multipoint relays that were selected unnecessarily.

The optimization is permissive: implementations do not have to use it. The RFC says it can, in some cases, create smaller and fewer messages without the opposite effect, and that optimized and unoptimized implementations interoperate.
sections.plainLanguage: A router may be able to remove some relays while keeping routes available. Using the option is not required and does not prevent communication with other implementations.

sections.title: When a Relay May Be Removed
sections.content:
A router starts with a routing MPR set selected under RFC 7181. It MAY remove selected relays when the sequence and metric-distance condition in this RFC is satisfied: the route through the existing MPR and the sequence of corresponding neighbors is shorter than the direct distance for each relay being considered.

The corresponding elements represent the same router, and the information needed for the decision is available from NHDP.
sections.plainLanguage: The router compares path metrics. If a path through a relay it already selected is shorter, it may remove additional relays from the set.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The update adds no protocol signals and does not change how received signals are processed. Removing an unneeded router from an MPR set also removes the need to include corresponding information in Topology Control messages.

The RFC says this change introduces no additional security considerations beyond those in RFC 7181.
sections.plainLanguage: The optimization changes local relay selection, not protocol signals. The RFC says it adds no security considerations.
